sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "And Yonasan said to him: Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, for your seat will be vacant," connecting it to the concept of nullification and the drawing down of a new light.

translations.translation: "And Yonasan said to him: Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, for your seat will be vacant."
And the Tzemach Tzedek explains in his maamar beginning with these words,
that Dovid
is the aspect of Malchus,
which includes all the souls of Israel,
for all of Israel are children of kings.
And the concept of "you will be missed, for your seat will be vacant" is,
that through the vacating
(the absence)
of the place of your seat,
[which is] nullification,
through this there will be "you will be missed,"
the drawing down of the remembrance
from above.
For remembrance is a very lofty aspect
(as will be explained below).
And this is the connection of "you will be missed, for your seat will be vacant" with "tomorrow is the new moon,"
because on the eve of Rosh Chodesh there is concealment and hiding of the moon,
until that in the moment before the molad not even a point remains of it,
and through this there is afterwards
(tomorrow)
a new month,
the renewed birth of the moon,
the drawing down of a new light from the sun to the moon,
which did not shine in it previously.
And so too is it with Israel, who are compared to the moon,
that through their nullification,
a most exalted light is drawn into them,
a new light.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the new light drawn down is called "remembrance," because it is the light of Ein Sof that is beyond relation to worlds, drawn specifically through nullification.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that this drawing down of the new light is called "you will be missed,"
[which is] remembrance,
because,
the drawing down of light that relates to worlds
(even a light that is above worlds but relates to worlds)
is not a true novelty,
and a new light is the light of Ein Sof that is beyond relation to worlds.
And this is that the drawing down of this light is called "you will be missed,"
because remembrance is in Ein Sof that is beyond relation to worlds.
And as explained elsewhere,
that just as in man the concept of remembrance applies only to something that is not significant in his eyes
(to the extent that it is easy to forget it),
so too is it above,
that the concept of remembrance is in Ein Sof that is beyond relation to worlds,
for everything before Him is considered as nothing.
And this is "you will be missed, for your seat will be vacant,"
that the drawing down of the light that is beyond relation to worlds
("you will be missed")
is specifically through nullification
("for your seat will be vacant").
For when a person's service is connected with his own existence
(an existence of holiness),
the drawing down that is drawn through the service is from the aspect of light that relates to worlds
(existence),
and in order for there to be a drawing down of the light that is beyond relation to worlds,
for everything before Him is considered as nothing,
it is through nullification,
"for your seat will be vacant."
